runs.quote: The NFA-A variant with 15% Al maintained ≈80% capacity after
100 cycles when compared with the NFA 811 (≈70%) and NFA-F

runs.text: (the NFA-F value is cut off in the text). The paper repeats that

runs.quote: the NFA-A variant had superior capacity retention

runs.text:
, the NFA-F curve is the lowest of the NFA variants at the end of the cycling test.

The document gives no mechanism for a retention advantage in NFA-F, because it reports none. Its contrast with NFA-F is in rate capability:

runs.quote: NFA-F variant delivered a low capacity of

runs.text: from the initial capacity. The authors also note that the iron-related redox couple

runs.quote: was depressed in the NFA-F variant

runs.text: , and they attribute the stability of NFA-A to its aluminum content:

runs.quote: we infer that the addition of 15%

runs.text:
aluminum offers good electrochemical stability and reversibility.

The document gives no further explanation for NFA-F's weaker cycling.

rendered:
The question's premise does not match the document. The paper does not name NFA-F as the best performer. It names NFA-A as the most stable variant: The NFA-A variant with 15% Al maintained ≈80% capacity after[1] 100 cycles when compared with the NFA 811 (≈70%) and NFA-F[2] (the NFA-F value is cut off in the text). The paper repeats that the NFA-A variant had superior capacity retention[3]. In Fig. 8[4], the NFA-F curve is the lowest of the NFA variants at the end of the cycling test.

The document gives no mechanism for a retention advantage in NFA-F, because it reports none. Its contrast with NFA-F is in rate capability: NFA-F variant delivered a low capacity of[5] at high rate, with in ≈27% loss[6] from the initial capacity. The authors also note that the iron-related redox couple was depressed in the NFA-F variant[7], and they attribute the stability of NFA-A to its aluminum content: we infer that the addition of 15%[8] aluminum offers good electrochemical stability and reversibility.

The document gives no further explanation for NFA-F's weaker cycling.
